newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: AMS gains, buoyed by resurgent optimism.
newsitem.headline: AMS gains, buoyed by resurgent optimism.

text.p: Shares of Austrian chip maker AMS surged almost six percent in early trade on the Vienna bourse, boosted by gains in U.S. semiconductor shares and expectations the worst might be behind for the troubled firm, traders said.
At 0910 GMT, Austria Mikro Systeme was up 43 schillings at 800, adding to Monday's five percent gain. The ATX index of 21 blue chips was up 4.01 points or 0.36 percent at the same time.
"The bad results have now been digested. There's a positive feeling about next year and we see some pretty large buy-orders particularly from abroad," said a trader.

The group's shares shed as much as 23 percent over the past month as investors anticipated a bleak set of nine-month earnings, depressed by the weak performance of AMS's subsidiaries in Germany and South Africa.

Market participants said the shares may recover to around 840 schillings in the near term as investors now believe the company will succeed in restructuring its loss-making units and will benefit from a global recovery in semiconductors.

"AMS has become a restructuring story. You can either believe in it or not. If you do, it's time to buy and have a good look at it," said another trader. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
